title: Move the CRM from hosted Postgres to local SQLite
description: The CRM is single-user local automation fed by local scrapes, but its store was a hosted Neon Postgres. That bought nothing: a network round trip per query, a credentials file, and a hard outage the moment the Neon database was deleted (verified: Prisma reports 'Authentication failed against database server'). SQLite matches the workload exactly (row-oriented, point lookups, real UNIQUE constraints) and is a one-line Prisma provider change. Prisma validates the existing schema unchanged under sqlite. The only code change is mode:'insensitive', which is Postgres-only; SQLite LIKE is already case-insensitive for ASCII so search behaviour is preserved.
acceptance_criteria: provider is sqlite, DATABASE_URL is a file path, no mode:'insensitive' remains, a migration exists, batch upsert and contacted toggle verified against the local file.
close_reason: Migrated to SQLite and verified end to end against the local file: batch upsert (2 new), idempotent re-sync (0 new / 2 updated, no duplicates), in-batch phone dedupe, string to float/int coercion, case-insensitive search across three casings, contacted toggle with contactedAt, and the unique phone constraint rejected at DB level.

title: CSV upload route repeats the find-then-create race
description: src/app/api/upload/route.ts still uses the findUnique-then-update-or-create pattern that was removed from the contacts batch endpoint: two serial round trips per row, and two concurrent uploads can both miss and the loser fails on the unique phone constraint. Replace with the same upsert-in-a-transaction shape.
acceptance_criteria: Upload route uses upsert; no read-then-write race remains in either write path.

title: Archive every scrape as an immutable Parquet file
description: A scrape is an observation at a point in time, but the batch upsert overwrites the previous observation for a given phone. Scrape a business today at 4.2 stars and again next month at 3.8 and the first reading is gone. Write each incoming batch to a timestamped append-only file (scrapes/<iso>_<query>.parquet) before it is projected into SQLite, so history accumulates and nothing is lost to an upsert. This is deliberately just an archive, not a query layer: pointing DuckDB at scrapes/*.parquet later needs no migration because the files are already there. Note DuckDB cannot UPDATE a Parquet file in place (verified: 'Binder Error: Can only update base table') which is exactly why the mutable contact state stays in SQLite.
acceptance_criteria: Every accepted batch leaves a Parquet file on disk; the file is never rewritten; SQLite remains the system of record for contacted/contactedAt/inviteCode.
